  [1] File: scripts/orchestrate_lib.py
      Problem: Lines: 785-804 (`PHASE_LABELS_PRIORITY`) and 805 (`TERMINAL_PHASES`); The nine new failure phase labels (`ai:clarify-failed`, `ai:plan-failed`, etc.) added to the label contract are missing from the orchestrator's phase priority list and terminal phase set.; `determine_phase()` relies on `PHASE_LABELS_PRIORITY` to identify the current state of an issue. If an issue is tagged with only a failure label, `determine_phase()` will return "no_labels". This causes the stall detector in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` to apply generic "no label" recovery actions (which have a shorter 60-minute threshold) instead of treating the failure as a terminal state requiring human intervention. Furthermore, because they are missing from `TERMINAL_PHASES`, the poller will not recognize these issues as finished, potentially leading to incorrect wave advancement logic.

An issue bearing only a failure label would return "no_labels", causing stall detection to treat it as a non-terminal phase and potentially trigger incorrect recovery actions (retriggers, escalations). These failure states are terminal and require human intervention; the misalignment prevents proper recognition. Additionally, TERMINAL_PHASES (line 805) is used to skip terminal issues in `detect_stalls()` (line 1064); absence means failure-labeled issues are never skipped, compounding the misbehavior.
